claims.text: Single-crystal FeNiCrMn initially forms an FCC solid solution.
The initial FeNiCrMn material is free of amorphous regions and has a low dislocation density.
The strain-rate-insensitive yield response is caused by rapid attainment of a critical dislocation-density threshold.
Attainment of the critical dislocation-density threshold triggers deformation-induced solid-state amorphization.
Thermally activated dislocation nucleation is not the dominant cause of yielding in this regime.
FCC-to-BCC transformation is not the primary deformation mode.
A critical dislocation density of approximately 8 × 10^15 m^-2 applies to amorphization in FeNiCrMn.
Amorphization localizes at intersections of deformation bands such as stacking faults or twins.
At low temperature and high strain rate, dislocations accumulate rapidly.
At the critical dislocation density, the free energy of heavily deformed FCC material becomes comparable to that of the amorphous phase.
The free-energy crossover causes a solid-state FCC-to-amorphous transformation.
Amorphization provides rapid, strain-rate-independent energy dissipation that masks the normal strain-rate sensitivity of dislocation glide.
Yield strength remains relatively constant as strain rate varies.
The local amorphous volume fraction increases sharply and nonlinearly after the critical dislocation density is exceeded.
Below approximately 600 K, amorphization begins at similar stress levels regardless of strain rate.
Above approximately 600 K, thermal recovery or dynamic recrystallization may dominate and restore strain-rate sensitivity.
Crystal-orientation anisotropy should be assessed by testing [100], [110], and [111] single crystals.
Using single crystals excludes grain-boundary slip as a deformation mechanism.
Traditional FCC Ni or Cu shows a significant yield-strength increase with strain rate due to thermally activated dislocation glide and does not amorphize at these strains.
Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 exhibits an FCC-to-BCC transformation that serves as a comparator for the falsification rule.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule says FCC-to-BCC transformation was seen in Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18, whereas the cited Ti-alloy record reports the opposite direction, BCC-to-FCC, during tension.
